title: ridgecrest-health-integration-call-notes-2026-05-22
content:
Call notes: Ridgecrest Health integration kickoff - 2026-05-22
Attendees: Maya Alvarez (Redwood SE), Owen Park (Redwood), Leah Kim (Redwood), Dr. Priya Nair (Ridgecrest IT), Samir Patel (Ridgecrest Product), Laura Gomez (Compliance)

Summary:
- High-level: Ridgecrest is evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for a pilot to power clinical note summarization and triage routing. Primary concerns: PHI handling, data residency (CA region), predictable latency for triage (<300ms p95 for short prompts), and auditability for compliance.
- They expect ~500k inference tokens/day in pilot, spiky during morning huddles. Long-term target: ~10M tokens/day across 3 hospitals.

Requirements / asks from Ridgecrest:
1) Data residency & networking
   - Need control plane and inference in their Azure CA region (they called out Canada Central).
   - Must deploy Private VPC with customer-managed peering (they will provision a transit gateway).
   - KMS integration mandatory (HSM prefered) for key management.
2) PHI / compliance
   - Automatic PII redaction is required on embedded exports. They want a configurable redaction layer pre-ingest into embeddings.
   - Audit logs for each request (request id, model version, prompt hash, response hash) with 7-year retention for pilot.
   - Role-based access for console + strict SSO (Okta) enforcement.
3) Latency / SLO
   - Target: p95 <= 300ms for 64-token prompts in triage; allowed burst up to 800ms. Need an approach for overload/fallback (model variant or cache warm).
4) Embeddings & search
   - Want sentence-transformer-style embeddings for clinical notes; exploring both semantic search and reranking.
   - Will run offline embeddings pipeline initially (nightly) but want realtime single-document embedding endpoint.
5) Model governance
   - Must be able to pin model version; require canary rollout capability + quick rollback.
6) Cost visibility
   - Show per-route token cost and ability to cap spend per project/team.

Technical gotchas / constraints uncovered in convo:
- Data format: they currently use HL7 FHIR bundles. We should confirm exact JSON payload shape; they likely will send full note text in an element but want to keep metadata (patient id) out of logs.
- EHR integration: their EHR sends base64 attachments for imaging captions - confirm size caps; might need chunking.
- Auth: they will proxy calls from internal backend service; plan is to use mutual TLS + token exchange to Redwood Private control plane. Need to validate MTLS requirements with infra team.
- Rate pattern: morning spike at 08:00-09:30 and evening triage; autoscaling policies must support sustained short bursts. Suggest warm-standby capacity for morning window.
- PII redaction: they want configurable ruleset (allow list for clinical codes, redact SSNs) - must confirm if they prefer Redwood-managed redaction or using their DLP product as a preprocessor.

Notes to self / SE concerns:
- We'll need a custom onboarding checklist: VPC peering, KMS key handshake, Okta SSO config, log sink (S3/GCS/Azure blob) for audit logs.
- Check: Azure region availability for our Private image and GPU SKU parity. If not available, discuss Dedicated with strict VPC egress controls.
- Embeddings model - propose rw-embed-clinical-v1 (if available); otherwise recommend open clinical embedding candidate + quantization profile for Private.
- Latency: consider colocating routing + KV cache inside customer VPC to hit 300ms; may need to size GPU (A10G/A100) depending on concurrency.

Action items / Next steps (owners + rough ETA):
- [Maya] Draft security checklist + onboarding doc for Ridgecrest (include required artefacts list) - due 2026-05-26.
- [Owen] Confirm Azure Canada Central availability for Private AMI + available GPU SKUs; open infra ticket - due 2026-05-24.
- [Leah] Put together model recommendation (embed + summarization) and expected cost estimates for pilot (tokens/day) - due 2026-05-27.
- [Samir / Ridgecrest] Share sample FHIR bundle sanitized (no PHI) and example note payloads - requested by 2026-05-25.
- [Maya] Schedule tech deep-dive (30-45m) with Ridgecrest infra + security to walk through peering/KMS/SSO - target 2026-05-28.
- [Laura / Ridgecrest Compliance] Provide explicit requirements for log retention and access controls (they mentioned 7-year retention but need formal policy) - due 2026-05-29.

Open questions to follow up on (to clarify on next call):
- Do they require HSM-backed encryption keys only, or will KMS with BYOK suffice?
- Confirm whether PII redaction must be handled before logs leave their network or if Redwood-managed redaction inside Private is acceptable.
- Expected concurrency for real-time requests during morning spike (requests/sec) - important for capacity planning.
- Any legal/regulatory constraints about model training on their data (they said no training, but need contractual wording).

Misc notes / conversation snippets:
- Priya: "We need a deterministic way to show we didn't retain PHI in logs" - highlight audit logs + prompt/response hashing as approach.
- Samir: "If latency spikes we need graceful fallback to a cheaper model, but accuracy mustn't drop below X" - need to quantify X (we asked for examples).

Draft email template to send after this call (copy for later):
Hi Samir/Priya/Laura,
Thanks for the kickoff today - attached are the notes and next steps. We'll send a short onboarding checklist and sample config for VPC peering + KMS. Can you confirm a preferred time for the tech deep-dive (we suggested 05-28)? Also please upload a sanitized FHIR bundle example to the Confluence page linked below.
Best,
Maya
